test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The freight and insurance paid for acquiring goods or for making them saleable is _______.

options.text: credited to the profit and loss account
debited to the profit and loss account

solution:
The correct answer is **debited to the trading account.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Freight and insurance paid for acquiring goods:**

 
 
• These costs are directly related to bringing the goods to the place of business and making them available for sale, which are part of the cost of goods sold.
 
• Debiting these expenses to the trading account aligns with the matching principle in accounting, which states that expenses should be matched with the revenues they help to generate.
 
• The trading account is used to calculate the gross profit or loss by comparing the cost of goods sold with sales revenue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Credited to the profit and loss account:**

 
 
• This is incorrect because profit and loss accounts are used for recording revenues and expenses that are not directly related to the cost of goods sold. Freight and insurance are directly related to the cost of goods sold.
 
 
 
• **Debited to the profit and loss account:**
 
 
• Incorrect because the profit and loss account deals with operating and non-operating expenses and incomes. Freight and insurance costs are part of the cost of acquiring goods, not operational expenses.
 
 
 
• **Credited to the trading account:**
 
 
• This is incorrect because the trading account is debited for costs that are incurred to bring goods to a saleable condition, not credited.
